To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NT3 activates Arf6 and that this activation is required for NT3-mediated neurite outgrowth.
NT3 activates Arf6 and that Rac1 activation is dependent on Arf6 activity.
NT3 induces Arf6 and RhoA activation in PC12 and N1E-115 cells, respectively, and that this activation is mediated by the activation of the TrkC receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of NT3 signaling in PC12 cells and primary sensory neurons, and the identification of NT3 downstream targets.
the identification of NT3 activated signaling pathways that lead to the regulation of cell movement.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of neurotrophins in the control of cell motility and membrane dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Arf6 activation in PC12 cells is mediated by TrkC, whereas the activation of Rac1 requires the presence of both TrkC and p75NTR.
NT3 activates Arf6 and Rho-family members, such as Rac1, through a mechanism that involves the sequential activation of the TrkC receptor and the PI3K-Akt pathway.
NT3 activates Arf6 and Rho family GTP-binding proteins via the Trk receptor and that the activation of Arf GTPases is cell type specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NT3 induces the activation of Arf-6 and Rac1 in a specific subset of cortical neurons, and that this activation is mediated by the NT3 receptor TrkC.
NT3, through the activation of TrkC, induces Arf6 activation and Rac-1 activation.
the NT3 receptor TrkC is able to activate the GTPases Arf6 and RhoA in a cell-type specific manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Arf6 and its effector, phospholipase D (PLD), are required for NT3-induced Rac1 activation and neurite outgrowth in PC12 cells.
Arf6 and its downstream effectors are activated in response to NT3 stimulation in a cell type-dependent manner.
